query: How would HelpfulnessNumerator change if reviews provided more detailed product information?

per_column.name: product_detail_depth
per_column.rationale: Directly operationalizes the treatment 'reviews provided more detailed product information' as an intervenable, settable property of the review content.

per_column.name: ingredient_or_nutrition_detail
per_column.rationale: A specific facet of detailed product information; an author can choose to include it, so it is intervenable and part of the treatment named in the query.

per_column.name: usage_instruction_present
per_column.rationale: Another intervenable facet of providing more detailed product information.

per_column.name: comparative_reference_present
per_column.rationale: Comparative detail is a settable component of the detail-depth treatment named in the query.

per_column.name: quantitative_detail_present
per_column.rationale: Quantitative detail is a facet of detailed product information; author-settable.

per_column.name: use_case_specificity
per_column.rationale: Specificity of use-case is a form of added product-information detail, intervenable by the author.

per_column.name: actionable_recommendation_present
per_column.rationale: Whether the review makes an actionable recommendation is more plausibly a consequence/co-feature of adding detail that then drives helpfulness, i.e. on the causal path rather than a common cause of both treatment and outcome.

per_column.name: review_length_tier
per_column.rationale: Longer reviews tend to contain more detail (affecting treatment) and independently attract more helpfulness votes (affecting outcome); a common cause not named in the query. Could partly be a mediator, but overall length is a plausible confounder driven by reviewer verbosity.

per_column.name: reviewer_expertise_signal
per_column.rationale: Expertise raises both the propensity to write detailed product info and the perceived helpfulness independent of detail; a classic common cause not named in the query.

per_column.name: sentiment_valence
per_column.rationale: Reviewer's underlying stance/experience can affect both how much detail is written and how helpful voters judge it; plausible common cause, not named in query.

per_column.name: product_category
per_column.rationale: Category shapes typical detail norms (e.g., supplements list ingredients) and baseline helpfulness voting; common cause not named in the query.

judge.rationale: The treatment 'more detailed product information' is intervenable (an author can choose to add ingredient, usage, comparative, quantitative, and use-case detail), and multiple added columns faithfully operationalize it. Crucially, the set includes several genuine confounders NOT named in the query — reviewer expertise, product category, and sentiment valence are all common causes of both writing detail and receiving helpfulness votes, demonstrating the capability under test. review_length_tier is a plausible (if partly mediating) confounder, and actionable_recommendation_present is better read as a mediator. Overall this realizes the what-if claim well.
